messages:
support-ash: FYI customer AcmeSearch reporting embeddings throughput drop this morning. tokens/sec looks stable, but vectors/sec is ~6x lower than baseline. customer says this started after a traffic split change. attaching their quick repro below.

customer-jordan: @support-ash yep, hit it around 08:10 UTC. Example call: `POST /v1/embeddings model=embed-large-8bit batch_size=128` -> 600 vectors/sec (expected ~3600). Same payload to hosted earlier returned ~3700 v/s. No auth errors, just slow.

support-ash: thanks. I grabbed our logs + a couple of prometheus queries. Short summary: overall request rate (rps) to that org is flat, token generation throughput (tokens/sec) from same model family is normal. GPU UTIL on the dedicated pool spiked for ~5m then dropped to ~10% despite queue depth being high. Strange.

eng-ml-ryan: can you paste the prometheus snippets and the nvidia-smi output? also curious about per-worker queue length and whether requests are being routed to a different model variant or fallback.

support-ash: pasted: 
```
# prom: vectors/sec by model_variant (last 15m)
sum(rate(embed_vectors{org=\"acme\"}[5m])) by (model_variant)
# results: embed-large-8bit: 600 vec/s, embed-large-fp16: 0 vec/s
# prom: tokens/sec steady ~120k tokens/s across other endpoints
# queue histogram (queue_depth) for pool dedicated-acme: 0-8: 40%, 9-32: 50%, >32: 10%
```

eng-runtime-lena: interesting that embed-large-fp16 shows 0. Are we sure routing didn't flip to a GPU-incompatible variant or to a node set with different binary (e.g., missing 8bit kernels)? Also queue depth skew suggests many requests are stacked but a few workers are consuming. can we check worker logs for continuous batching window/timeouts?

support-ash: good call. I grabbed a sample worker stack trace and this line appears repeatedly: `kvcache_miss=true evict_count=12 batch_wait_ms=50` and `fallback_variant=embed-large-8bit->embed-large-fp16 reason=kernel-mismatch` in the infra logs around 08:09.

eng-sre-matt: kernel-mismatch fallback could cause a significant perf delta. If hosts don't have the optimized 8bit kernels, we fall back to fp16 path which is slower per vector and may reduce concurrency. But customer said tokens/sec fine — maybe because tokenized generation uses a different runtime path. We should confirm binary versions on hosts that served acme.

infra-bot: node-assignment: worker-56 served 78% of acme requests between 08:09-08:14 UTC. image: inference-runtime v2.3.1, kernel-plugins: [fp16, reference], 8bit-plugin: MISSING.

eng-ml-ryan: that explains it. No 8bit plugin => requests that prefer 8bit got diverted or fell back. That would decrease vectors/sec and increase queueing as each request uses more GPU time. Next steps: 1) confirm routing rule change (traffic split) 2) check if the rollback put traffic on a host pool missing 8bit kernels 3) reproduce locally with same image.

support-ash: confirmed from audit: at 08:05 we added a temporary route to pool `dedicated-acme-2` (reason: capacity burst). That pool was created from autoscale and uses image `inference-runtime v2.3.1` but built without the 8bit plugin (packaging bug).

eng-runtime-lena: plan: roll forward by installing 8bit plugin on the nodes in `dedicated-acme-2` OR shift traffic back to `dedicated-acme` which has the correct image. Which is safer for customer?

customer-jordan: prefer quick fix that doesn't require changing our client. If shifting back to original pool avoids downtime, do that. We need throughput restored ASAP, SLA impacted.

eng-sre-matt: safe mitigation: 1) pause routing to dedicated-acme-2 (traffic -> original pool) 2) mark dedicated-acme-2 as draining until image is fixed 3) follow up to bake 8bit plugin into the autoscale image. I'll coordinate the rollback now.

support-ash: rolling traffic back now. `kubectl patch svc routing/acme-split -p '{"spec":{"weights":{"dedicated-acme":0.9,"dedicated-acme-2":0.1}}'` -> updating to 0.98/0.02 then 1.0/0.0.

eng-ml-ryan: while that's happening, can someone collect: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,mem_utilization --format=csv -l 5` for the affected nodes and `grep -E \"kvcache|fallback_variant\" /var/log/inference/*.log | tail -n 200`? I'd like a before/after snapshot to show improvement.

support-ash: collected before/after. After traffic moved back (08:18): embed-large-8bit vec/s -> ~3500, queue_depth >32 dropped to 0%, GPU util stabilized at 70-85% across workers. logs show kvcache_miss count dropped and no fallback_variant lines.

eng-runtime-lena: great. Action items: 
- eng-sre to keep dedicated-acme-2 drained and update autoscale image (add 8bit plugin)
- eng-ml to add a check in routing that verifies required kernels/plugins present before sending traffic (preflight)
- support to notify customer and confirm SLA remediation

eng-sre-matt: filing infra ticket INFRA-6321 to bake plugin into AMI and ensure autoscale builds include it. tagging eng-runtime-lena.

support-ash: customer updated: throughput restored after rollback. customer asked for postmortem and preventative steps. I'll draft.

eng-ml-ryan: for the postmortem include reproducible steps we used: 
1) reproduce: send steady RPS of real payloads to embed-large-8bit on pool X (batch_size 128) and measure vectors/sec with `prometheus` query and `curl` latency headers
2) check worker plugin list via `/internal/host/plugins` endpoint
3) check logs for `fallback_variant` and `kvcache` patterns

support-ash: tagging PM and ops for postmortem. Closing thread once postmortem link shared. :white_check_mark:

customer-jordan: thanks team, appreciate the quick rollback and updates.

eng-runtime-lena: follow-up: adding a CI check so autoscale AMI builds run a small embed workload to validate plugin presence.

support-ash: nice. I'll attach the postmortem draft in a separate thread.
